title: bug: packetManifest never reports a declared but unserved protected-check overlay (task.requiredCheckSnapshot)
description:
CQ-V01 (task-bde86540) handed this forward. It was still unowned at CQ-V12's whole-epic review (task-b621ddc9, worker-0e1ab990, 2026-11-01). No C-series row owns it: a board search for packetManifest finds only the docs-only CQ-C11a. The delivery gate fails closed (protected-checks-unapproved), so this is an observability gap for agents, not a bypass.

Defect:
- context/contextPacket.ts:17-18 makes task.requiredCheckSnapshot "Mandatory when served (the approved protected-check overlay); never reported missing".
- tools/getContext.ts:556 serves it only when readRequiredCheckSnapshot(task) binds.
- So a task can declare executionContract.requiredChecks while its snapshot is absent, malformed, or bound to other definitions. That task gets a packet with no overlay, and the packet manifest does not flag the gap.
- The worker or QA seat cannot tell from the manifest that the protected check bytes are missing. Meanwhile delivery reports protected-checks-unapproved.

Failing-test sketch:
- A task with non-empty executionContract.requiredChecks and no requiredCheckSnapshot (or a mismatched one): expect packetManifest to list task.requiredCheckSnapshot with status missing (mandatory, and a reason such as unbound-snapshot).
- Today it lists nothing.
- A task without requiredChecks must still list nothing.
definitionOfDone: When executionContract.requiredChecks is non-empty and readRequiredCheckSnapshot returns null, get_context's packetManifest reports task.requiredCheckSnapshot as missing (mandatory)
Tasks without requiredChecks are unchanged, and a served snapshot stays mandatory and is never role-trimmed or truncated
contextPacket/getContext tests cover both cases; the docs/MCP_SERVER.md packetManifest text matches; cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test passes

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first, then the fix. Every vitest/npm run happens in a git-archive snapshot, never in the shared checkout (global rail).

**Fix**, in packages/moe-daemon/src/context/contextPacket.ts only (getContext.ts stays untouched). buildPacketManifest stays pure over the assembled body.
- Today the loop over CONDITIONAL_SECTIONS lists 'task.requiredCheckSnapshot' only when it is servable.
- Add one more case. When it is NOT served and the body's own `task.executionContract.requiredChecks` is a non-empty array, push `{ path: 'task.requiredCheckSnapshot', mandatory: true, status: 'missing', reason: 'unbound-snapshot' }`.
  - Read it with the existing own() helper, so an inherited name reads as absent.
  - getContext.ts:556-593 serves the snapshot only when readRequiredCheckSnapshot binds it, and always serves a set executionContract. So this fires exactly when requiredChecks are declared and readRequiredCheckSnapshot returned null: the snapshot is absent, malformed, or bound to other definitions.
- Smallest shape: map each conditional section to the body path that makes it required (e.g. `{ 'task.requiredCheckSnapshot': 'task.executionContract.requiredChecks' }`), or a one-line predicate for the single entry.
- A missing section adds nothing to mandatoryChars. `complete` turns false through the existing every-served rule.
- Update the CONDITIONAL_SECTIONS doc comment, which today says "never reported missing": the section is mandatory when served, and missing (unbound-snapshot) when requiredChecks are declared but no bound snapshot is served.
- Error handling: no new throw. A non-array or empty requiredChecks is not a declaration, and an odd body shape still reads as missing or absent, as today.

**Tests**, in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContextPacket.test.ts, with toStrictEqual like the file's existing tests.
- Pure builder, next to the 'odd shapes' test. With the snapshot unserved:
  - requiredChecks [{...}] → the missing section with reason 'unbound-snapshot', complete false, mandatoryChars unchanged by it;
  - requiredChecks [], absent, `{}`, `'x'`, or inherited via the prototype → no snapshot section.
  - A served snapshot is still `served` and mandatory, with or without requiredChecks.
- Through get_context: seed `executionContract: { ...CONTRACT, requiredChecks: [{ id: 'unit', command: 'npm test', scripts: ['scripts/check.sh'] }] }`.
  - (a) No requiredCheckSnapshot.
  - (b) A well-formed snapshot whose definitionDigest is for OTHER definitions.
  - Both: `res.task` has no requiredCheckSnapshot, the manifest lists the unbound-snapshot section, and complete is false. Check every caller of the file's first it.each (worker-w, qa-q, architect-a, governor-g, '') in the default view, so it is never role-trimmed.
  - (c) A bound snapshot: `{ version: 1, revision: 'a'.repeat(40), definitionDigest: definitionDigest(validateExecutionContract(contract)!.requiredChecks!), entries: [{ path: 'scripts/check.sh', oid: 'b'.repeat(40) }] }`, digesting the definitions exactly as readRequiredCheckSnapshot does. It is served whole (toStrictEqual to the stored value) and listed served and mandatory for every caller in BOTH views. budget.mandatoryChars includes its JSON length.
  - Imports: definitionDigest from ../delivery/requiredChecks.js; validateExecutionContract from ../state/validators.js. Importing is fine; editing validators.ts is not needed.
- The existing first test keeps pinning "no requiredChecks → no snapshot section" unchanged; do not weaken it.
- Run the new rows once BEFORE the fix: (a), (b) and the declared builder row must fail.

**Iterate in a snapshot**, from the repo root:
- Create it: `S=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-435e8989-XXXXXX) && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S"`.
- After each edit: `cp --parents packages/moe-daemon/src/context/contextPacket.ts packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContextPacket.test.ts "$S"`.
- Once: `cd "$S/packages/moe-daemon" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`.
- Then, under the same env -i: `npx vitest run src/tools/getContextPacket.test.ts src/delivery/requiredChecks.snapshot.test.ts src/context/contextDelta.test.ts`.
implementationPlan.note: Red first: builder, (a), (b) failed pre-fix; green after. tsc clean; 141 tests pass across the 3 files in a snapshot. Dirty peer paths untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Docs, in docs/MCP_SERVER.md with the Edit tool. Change only these two sentences. Another open task may also declare this file; the Edit tool's witness lands it, so never use a shell write.
- moe.get_context paragraph (~line 190), which ends "... and omitted otherwise.": add that packetManifest then lists it `missing` with reason `unbound-snapshot` whenever the contract declares `requiredChecks`.
- Packet manifest paragraph (~line 308): replace "`task.requiredCheckSnapshot` is listed only when served." with the new rule. It is listed `served` (mandatory, never role-trimmed or truncated) when served. When the contract declares `requiredChecks` but no snapshot bound to them is served (absent, malformed, or bound to other definitions), it is listed `missing` with reason `unbound-snapshot`. Otherwise it is not listed.
- docs/SCHEMA.md's PacketManifest shape has no reason enum, so it needs no change.
implementationPlan.note: Two doc sentences updated via Edit tool.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: get_context's packetManifest lists task.requiredCheckSnapshot as missing (mandatory, reason 'unbound-snapshot') whenever the served task.executionContract declares a non-empty requiredChecks array but no snapshot bound to those definitions is served. A served snapshot stays listed served and mandatory, never role-trimmed or truncated. A task without requiredChecks gets exactly today's manifest.
acceptanceCriteria: Declared requiredChecks with no stored snapshot, or with one bound to other definitions: the manifest has {path:'task.requiredCheckSnapshot', mandatory:true, status:'missing', reason:'unbound-snapshot'} and complete false, for every caller role.
A bound snapshot is served whole and listed served and mandatory, in both views and for every role.
No requiredChecks (absent, empty, or not an array): no snapshot section, exactly as today.
docs/MCP_SERVER.md describes the rule; the full daemon suite and tsc pass in a snapshot.
invariants: buildPacketManifest stays pure and never throws; it reads only own properties of the assembled body.
The manifest never grants approval, readiness or evidence; delivery still fails closed with protected-checks-unapproved.
getContext.ts serving rules are unchanged: the snapshot is still served only when readRequiredCheckSnapshot binds it.
compatibility: Manifests of tasks without requiredChecks are byte-identical, so existing packetId digests for those tasks are unchanged.
PacketSection's shape is unchanged; only a new reason string, 'unbound-snapshot', appears.
approvedScope: context/contextPacket.ts: the conditional-section branch and its doc comment.
tools/getContextPacket.test.ts: builder rows and get_context rows (a), (b), (c).
reuse: delivery/requiredChecks.ts definitionDigest and state/validators.ts validateExecutionContract in tests, to build a bound snapshot exactly as readRequiredCheckSnapshot checks it.
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-daemon/src/context/contextPacket.ts:17-18 CONDITIONAL_SECTIONS = ['task.requiredCheckSnapshot'], skipped when not servable (buildPacketManifest loop).
packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContext.ts:556 serves requiredCheckSnapshot only when readRequiredCheckSnapshot(task) is non-null; :590 serves executionContract whenever it is set.

packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/requiredChecks.ts:128 readRequiredCheckSnapshot returns null unless the definitions are non-empty and the digest, revision (40 hex), entry shape and order all match; it never throws.
